turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I broke my arm on Wednesday and now my whole weekend is ruined.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Oh no, I'm sorry. How are you feeling?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right, next thing. My old bathroom extractor fan is basically just noise now, and I have a few ways to deal with it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you hold your comments till I've gone through every choice? I'll tell you when I'm done.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could just clean it properly, take the cover off and get all the dust out of the blades.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or buy a cheap replacement fan from the hardware store and fit it into the same hole myself.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Or pay an electrician to put in a proper quiet fan with a humidity sensor.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's everything. Which one would you pick?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: How old is the fan? A really old motor won't get quieter with cleaning. In that case, the electrician option costs more but you'll never think about it again.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sore and fed up. I was supposed to go kayaking.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's rotten luck. Could you still go along with your friends and enjoy the riverbank, maybe with a picnic?
